messages:
acme-eng: hey, heads up — our rerank responses started returning strange values earlier today. scores are large negative floats, not 0-1. example in payload below.

maya-cs: sorry about that — can you paste the request (no secrets) and the raw response?

acme-eng: here you go (sanitized):
```json
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer ****
{
  "model": "redwood/rerank-v1",
  "query": "best battery choices",
  "candidates": ["AA", "AAA", "18650"]
}
```
response: 
```json
{
  "scores": [-123.45, -5.6, -0.12],
  "meta": {"units": "raw_logit"}
}
```
acme-eng: noticed latency spikes too ~3-6s per call, and once got a 401 after a retry. billing dashboard showed an odd token spike (possible duplicate retries).

maya-cs: thanks. a few things: 1) rerank returns unnormalized logits by default (so negatives expected). 2) latency + 401 could explain duplicate retries inflating tokens. 3) we should confirm client-side assume-probabilities behavior.

alex-ml: confirming — our reranker outputs logits (arbitrary real numbers). Clients must apply softmax or use the SDK helper normalize=true flag. Quick softmax snippet: 
```python
import math
def softmax(scores):
    e = [math.exp(s - max(scores)) for s in scores]
    s = sum(e)
    return [x/s for x in e]
```

sam-runtime: on the runtime side I see a few 5xxs and a couple auth flaps around 2026-03-15T14:02Z for that org id, likely due to a token rotation attempt. I flagged the node that handled their traffic — it had elevated GC pauses causing 3-4s tail latency. I'm rolling a GC tuning patch now.

acme-eng: ok thanks. two follow-ups: how should we interpret negative magnitude? client thought -100 meant low probability but -0.1 meant high.

alex-ml: magnitude is relative across candidates. The softmax is invariant to adding constants, so absolute negative values don't map to probability directly. Example: [-123, -5, -0.1] -> softmax will make the largest (least negative) the highest prob. Don't normalize by dividing by a range — use softmax.

maya-cs: for immediate mitigation, you can either: 1) set normalize=true in SDK call (will return probs), or 2) apply the softmax post-call. We'll add a note to hit in our docs.

acme-eng: about tokens — can you confirm retries were counted? we saw token jump from retries.

billing-bot: automated notice: we detected 2 repeated requests from api-key ending in abcd that matched within 1s window; duplicate billing protection not applicable for rerank endpoint. Billing team aware, will follow up.

sam-runtime: GC patch rolled to the problematic node; I'll keep monitoring. Also recommending client enable exponential backoff to avoid retry storms when they see 401/5xx.

acme-eng: thanks — we'll switch to normalize=true for now and add backoff. Please keep us posted on uptime. :thumbsup:

maya-cs: tracking this as CS-7891. action items: alex to add docs note about logits vs probs; sam to monitor runtime patch impact; billing to review duplicate charge exemptions.

alex-ml: I'll add a short snippet and a FAQ entry today. :memo:

sam-runtime: monitoring dashboards show p95 latency dropping to 200-300ms after patch on that node, will update by EOD. :chart_with_downwards_trend
